key_insight: Rigid nozzles maximize thrust amplification, while flexible nozzles deliver better impulse-per-energy efficiency through deformation-driven flow control.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a design trade-off map for pulsed-jet propulsion, helping engineers choose between peak performance and energy-efficient actuation in bioinspired underwater systems.
method: Comparison of rigid vs. flexible nozzle geometries
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 5x impulse for rigid nozzles, about 2.5x for flexible nozzles, and a maximum normalized impulse-to-energy ratio for flexible designs about 1.8x higher than rigid ones.
watch_item: Results come from simulation-based optimization, so experimental validation and manufacturability of the flexible deformation profiles remain important concerns.
paper_title: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization of rigid and flexible nozzles for energy-efficient pulsed jet propulsion
